verdicts.question: What are Bengaluru's standing entry hours and no-entry rules for goods vehicles (city-wide, not temporary notices)? What do local transporters and Porter/Vahak charge per km and for loading for mini-trucks and tempos?
verdicts.problems: Verification limits first: no cited source could be reached this session (WebSearch budget was already exhausted at 200/200 before the first query; WebFetch and curl are refused for every host by the egress proxy), so none of the 20 sources is confirmed by snippet. What I could check: (1) Arithmetic holds — a 07:00–11:00 and 16:00–22:00 ban leaves 11:00–16:00 and 22:00–07:00; a 10:00/10:30–14:30 and 16:30–21:00 Saturday ban leaves 14:30–16:30 and 21:00–10:00. The MVA s.2 thresholds quoted (LMV up to 7,500 kg GVW, HGV over 12,000 kg, MGV in between) match the Act as I know it. (2) The repo's own independent read of BTP's Kannada notices on 29 Sep 2026 (docs/plan/research/handoff/briefs-raw/logistics.json, findings[8]) CONTRADICTS a key framing in this answer: it records the Electronic City elevated tollway restriction as dated 11–30 Sep and the Peenya elevated corridor restriction as 4–30 Sep, with reasons given as repairs, resurfacing and load tests that 'change month to month' — not standing orders 'until further orders'. It also lists Peenya as goods-autos-only (no 07–11/16–22 medium/heavy window) and does not mention the Silk Board–Ragigudda decker barring anything beyond HGVs 24 h. So the answer's corridor list may already be lapsed or changed on pilot day (13 Oct 2026); the decision must treat corridor bans as a month-by-month admin table, which the brief itself recommends. (3) The October regime (HGVs barred 07:00–22:00 'from next month', 8–16 t and above-16 t tiers, transshipment hubs, milk/vegetable exemption) rests on one Public TV interview (25 Sep 2026) plus one Asianet Newsable draft story (15 Jul 2026); neither is confirmed by snippet and no notification is cited — the answer says so, which is right, but the decision should not build routes on the 8–16 t tier at all until a gazette/BTP order exists. (4) Porter starting fares (₹150 e-loader to ₹330 Pickup 8 ft; Tata Ace ₹230) are corroborated only by the repo's own 29 Sep read of porter.in (same page, same day) — not an independent snippet. The Porter FAQ figures (60-minute free loading, ₹50 cancellation, 5% GST under RCM, Load Assist extra) are plausible but not confirmed by snippet. (5) Vahak '10 lakh+ transporters, 850+ cities' is corroborated by the repo's 29 Sep read of vahak.in only. (6) Local-transporter rate ranges (₹25–45/km, ₹5–8/min waiting, ₹390 driver loading, ₹400–800 per helper, Tata 407 ₹500 base + ₹50/km) come from movers' marketing pages (one dated 2025-09-29, three undated) — not confirmed by snippet and not benchmarks for scrap loads, which are heavier per trip and often need a helper; the answer already labels them as marketing figures. (7) Refined-chain gap: the answer models only 'yard-to-recycler-to-manufacturer' HGV legs. The founder's chain inserts a pre-processor (S3 bales → S4–S7 flake/granule/crumb) and a compounder, adds dry-waste centres/MRFs, authorised waste handlers and TSDFs, and makes every processing record emit by-product and residual lots as separate consignments. Logistics facts that follow and are missing here: residual/hazardous lots (e-waste fractions, battery electrolyte, used oil, tyre pyrolysis char, PCB residue) may move only on a KSPCB-authorised transporter with a HOWM Rules 2016 manifest (Form 10) and, for hazardous waste, GPS-tracked vehicles — a kabadiwala's goods auto or a Porter Ace is not a lawful vehicle for those lots; S3 bale loads (yard → pre-processor) are the first leg where an HGV and the city ban bite, so the timing rule applies from S3 onward, while S0–S2 legs (household → kabadiwala → yard) are light-vehicle legs at any hour; freight should be recorded as a per-lot cost between price levels L2/L3 and L3/L4 so that L3 (pre-processor to yard) can be quoted delivered or ex-works; and e-way bills (motor-vehicle loads over ₹50,000, CGST Rule 138) attach to the same lots.
verdicts.correction: Standing city-wide rule (as reported 3–4 Aug 2024 by Deccan Herald and Public TV, not re-confirmed this session): heavy goods vehicles (over 12 t GVW under MVA s.2(16)) may not move in Bengaluru 07:00–11:00 and 16:00–22:00 Mon–Fri and Sunday, and roughly 10:00/10:30–14:30 and 16:30–21:00 on Saturdays; allowed windows are therefore 11:00–16:00 and 22:00–07:00 weekdays, 14:30–16:30 and 21:00–10:00 Saturdays. Light goods vehicles up to 7.5 t GVW (goods autos, Tata Ace, 8-ft pickups, most Tata 407/Eicher variants) are outside that ban on surface roads; medium goods vehicles (7.5–12 t) are an open item for BTP. Corridor bans are NOT standing: the repo's 29 Sep read of BTP's Kannada notices dates the Electronic City tollway restriction 11–30 Sep and the Peenya corridor 4–30 Sep for repair/load-test reasons that change monthly; only the BGS flyover and Silk Board–Ragigudda decker HGV bans read as round-the-clock. Keep an admin-edited 'corridor restrictions' table and re-read btp.karnataka.gov.in the week of 13 Oct rather than hard-coding any corridor. A 07:00–22:00 HGV ban 'from October' is a single unconfirmed news claim (Public TV, 25 Sep 2026) on top of a July draft; plan the S3-onward heavy legs for 22:00–07:00 as the safe default and treat 11:00–16:00 as a bonus window until BTP publishes an order. Prices: Porter publishes only starting fares in Bengaluru (₹150 e-loader 350 kg, ₹205 3-wheeler 500 kg, ₹230 Tata Ace 750 kg, ₹330 Pickup 8 ft — same-day repo read of porter.in, not independently confirmed); per-km, helper and waiting rates come only from an in-app quote. Vahak is a bidding load board (claims 10 lakh+ transporters), fit for yard → pre-processor → recycler lots, not on-demand pickups. Local mover pages quote Tata Ace ₹250–255 base then ₹25–45/km plus ₹5–8/min waiting and ₹400–800 per helper; treat these as unverified marketing ranges and replace them with 10 phone quotes from scrap-yard transporters before pricing anything. Refined-chain additions: S0–S2 legs ride on light vehicles at any hour; S3 bale legs and S4–S7 feedstock legs are the HGV/timing legs; every residual or hazardous lot from a processing record (e-waste fractions, battery electrolyte, used oil, pyrolysis char, PCB residue) must travel on a KSPCB-authorised transporter with a HOWM Rules Form 10 manifest (GPS-tracked for hazardous waste) — never on a kabadiwala auto or Porter vehicle; record freight per lot between L2/L3 and L3/L4 and attach the e-way bill (Rule 138, over ₹50,000) to the same lot. Status: partly. Open items: BTP October order and MGV treatment; live Porter quote; corridor table refresh on 12 Oct; KSPCB-authorised transporter list and rates for hazardous lots.

verdicts.question: Can a startup use ULIP (the government's logistics data platform) to check transporters' vehicles and drivers, and what does access require?
verdicts.problems: No source could be reached this session (WebSearch budget exhausted at 200/200 before the first query; WebFetch and curl blocked for every host including pib.gov.in and goulip.in), so nothing here is confirmed by snippet; the repo has no earlier read of ULIP either (logistics.md line 63 records it as 'not checked'). Given that, the answer's structure is sound but several load-bearing operational figures rest on a single non-official how-to (NirmanKit, 25 Jun 2026): ₹0 government fees, 3–5 working days review, ₹100 stamp-paper NDA, 7–14 working days to sandbox, GSTIN-matching eligibility. None is in a PIB release the answer cites, and goulip.in itself (per the answer) publishes no fee — so the decision's 'sandbox before 13 Oct' timeline is unsupported. The PIB figures (1,300+ companies, 350+ agreements, 43 systems/11 ministries/129 APIs, 100 crore+ transactions as of 19 Mar 2025; the 2022 seven-step process) are consistent with what I know of ULIP's public releases but not confirmed by snippet, and they are 18 months old — a newer PIB count likely exists. The API field lists (VAHAN/01–03, SARATHI/01, base URL ulip.dpiit.gov.in/ulip/v1.0.0, 30-minute token expiry) come from Scribd uploads and a third-party GitHub README, i.e. unofficial copies of possibly outdated integration guides. The MoRTH data-sharing policy (Aug 2025) and its consent/masking regime are plausible and the answer correctly flags that its effect on ULIP's VAHAN/SARATHI responses is unpublished — this is the single biggest unknown and it can invalidate the whole cut-over plan (if owner name/DL name are masked, ULIP cannot verify a Saathi). The IFF piece (23 Sep 2026) and EKO prices (RC ₹3.00, DL ₹1.80, setup from ₹6,000) are not confirmed by snippet; EKO's per-call prices are fine as a budget placeholder but the decision commits to 'EKO-class' vendor prices as if settled. Not mentioned: DPDP Rules 2025 (notified Nov 2025) phase in consent-notice duties, and a KYC vendor pulling Vahan/Sarathi data on the platform's behalf still needs the driver's consent under the MoRTH policy — the answer's 'in-app driver consent' should be an explicit consent record per lookup. Refined-chain gap: verification must cover more than 'transporter vehicle and Saathi driver'. Pre-processors, e-waste dismantlers, battery breakers, used-oil re-refiners, TSDFs and authorised waste handlers must hold KSPCB authorisation/registration (HOWM Rules 2016, E-Waste Rules 2022, Battery Rules 2022, CPCB EPR portals), and vehicles carrying residual or hazardous lots need transporter authorisation and GPS — ULIP has no API for any of that, so the admin's verification checklist per role needs a KSPCB/CPCB-registration step that this answer does not mention. Also, driver checks for hazardous-lot transporters should include a hazardous-goods endorsement on the DL (SARATHI/01 'class of vehicle/badge' may or may not expose it — open item).
verdicts.correction: Yes in principle: ULIP (goulip.in, NICDC Logistics Data Services Ltd under DPIIT) is open to private companies, and PIB's releases (1 Oct 2022 process description; 19 Mar 2025 count of 1,300+ registered companies and 129 APIs — neither re-confirmed this session) describe the route: register, submit a use case, review, sign an NDA, integrate, security check, then live data via VAHAN/01 (vehicle number → owner, RC status, class, fitness, insurance, PUCC) and SARATHI/01 (DL number + DOB → name, status, validity, class). Everything about fees, timelines, NDA format and eligibility (₹0 fee, 3–5 day review, ₹100 stamp paper, 7–14 days to sandbox) comes from one third-party how-to and must be treated as unverified until NLDSL's helpdesk (1800 309 8908 / Helpdesk@goulip.in) confirms it in writing; do not plan the 13 Oct pilot around a ULIP sandbox. The decisive open question is whether, after MoRTH's Aug 2025 National Transport Repository data-sharing policy, ULIP's VAHAN/SARATHI responses are masked or require the data principal's Aadhaar-OTP consent; if masked, ULIP cannot verify identity and only confirms RC/DL validity. Pilot default: the admin verifies each transporter's RC and each Saathi's DL by viewing the driver's own mParivahan/DigiLocker record in person (free, no API, lawful), records last-4 digits, validity dates and a verified flag, and takes explicit consent per lookup; a licensed KYC API (EKO-class, quoted at about ₹3 per RC and ₹1.80 per DL plus GST — not confirmed this session) is an optional accelerator, never a scraped-data app. Refined-chain additions: the admin's per-role checklist must also verify KSPCB authorisation for pre-processors handling regulated streams, e-waste dismantlers, battery breakers, used-oil re-refiners, TSDFs and authorised waste handlers, and transporter authorisation plus GPS for vehicles carrying residual/hazardous lots — none of which ULIP provides; source those from KSPCB/CPCB registration portals and record the authorisation number and expiry on the business profile. Status: needs-pilot-or-counsel. Open items: ULIP fee/timeline in writing; masking/consent status of VAHAN/SARATHI after the MoRTH policy; whether SARATHI/01 exposes a hazardous-goods endorsement; DPDP consent wording (counsel).
